title: Monitoring probe fails after a routine redeploy: 'Operation not permitted' opening a raw socket
description_md:
The on-box monitoring agent runs as the unprivileged `netmon` service account (no sudo) and uses a small helper, `/usr/local/bin/icmp-probe`, to build a raw ICMP packet directly for a lightweight latency check -- deliberately not running as root or shelling out to a setuid `ping`. It's been working fine for months, but after last night's routine redeploy of the monitoring-agent package, `netmon`'s probe now fails immediately with `Operation not permitted` -- even though `ls -l /usr/local/bin/icmp-probe` shows it's still owned by root and still executable, identical to before. SSH in as `trainee` (passwordless `sudo`), work out what the redeploy actually changed, and get the probe working for `netmon` again.

You're done when running `icmp-probe` as the `netmon` user succeeds and prints its probe-ok marker.
